text:
samir desai: hey hi! just got my M3 Pro MBP from mailroom. followed the Quick Start (Apple Business Manager + Kandji). enrollment shows 'Device in ABM but not activated'. System prompts about 'Profile installation failed: Certificate chain incomplete' and when i try to enable FileVault it errors: 'Escrow failed: unable to reach escrow server'. Okta DDI shows device untrusted. anyone seen this? wondering if i missed a step or need a CAC cert installed
it-desk: welcome samir :wave: can you confirm if you used the activation lock code flow with Apple Configurator or if this was DEP automatic activation? also which network were you on during setup (corp vs home)?
samir desai: DEP/ABM automatic from FedEx box -> powered on and connected to my home wifi. didn't touch configurator. network was my home ISP.

rachel wong: likely the intermediate CA didn't get pushed during enrollment on non-corp networks; we enforce our PKI via profile and SCEP during bootstrap. quick checks pls:
```
profiles status -type configuration
scutil --proxy
sudo fdesetup status
```
and also check Keychain Access -> Certificates for 'Redwood Corporate CA' presence
devops-bot: automated note: if system date/time is NTP-off, SCEP cert issuance can fail. run `sudo systemsetup -getnetworktimeserver` and `sudo systemsetup -getusingnetworktime`
samir desai: ran commands, pasted outputs:
profiles: Enrolled to kandji: true; profiles: com.redwood.mdm present, com.redwood.security missing
scutil --proxy: no proxy set
sudo fdesetup status: FileVault is Off
sudo systemsetup -getusingnetworktime: Network Time: On

it-desk: thanks. com.redwood.security missing explains Okta. can you open Safari and try visiting https://pki.redwood.internal (will redirect to cert push). if that fails, try reconnecting to RWD-Corp SSID - our onboarding ACL allows SCEP traffic. if you're not near office, we can push the missing intermediate from Kandji console but that requires the serial last 4.
rachel wong: before we push, one more trick: reboot while on your ISP with Ethernet or hotspot sometimes breaks SCEP; if you switch to tethering from phone it can help. otherwise we can do a remediation push. do you want temporary admin while we triage (2hr window)? it can speed approvals for kernel/system extensions needed by VPN client
samir desai: i can come into office later today but would prefer remote fix. ok for temp admin, yes please. last 4 serial: C9A2
it-desk: temporary admin granted for 3 hours starting now. pushing remediation to Kandji to install com.redwood.security profile and corporate CA. creating ticket TKT-20260318-77 and tagging endpoint. please stay online for ~10 minutes while we push.
devops-bot: remediation attempt: push_profile(com.redwood.security) -> queued -> delivered to device (status: unknown)
rachel wong: i see the device in console as 'profile pending'. two things: open System Settings -> Privacy & Security and allow any 'System Extension Blocked' banners; then check Keychain Access for Corporate CA. after that run `profiles renew -type enrollment` and `sudo fdesetup enable` to trigger escrow once profile present.
samir desai: allowed two system extension prompts, found no certificate in Keychain still. ran profiles renew -> error 'renewal failed: scep server unreachable'.
it-desk: ok looks like SCEP failed due to home ISP blocking UDP/TTL weirdness occasionally. i'll escalate to network team to try alternate PV. in the meantime we enabled a one-time manual escrow via our portal — samir, try FileVault enable now and the portal will give a recovery key to paste (we audit this)
samir desai: used portal flow and pasted recovery key, fdesetup says FileVault On. Okta still shows non-compliant until the profile installs.
rachel wong: profile installed a few mins later (console shows success). can you run `profiles status -type configuration` and confirm com.redwood.security present?
samir desai: yes now present. Okta shows compliant after sync. thx all! huge help :raised_hands:
